data_pull.method: identity-filtered, bounded pull: 300 episode files/day from the 2 most recent days, downloaded one at a time, matched against a target set built from the top 150 leaderboard rows (350 names/usernames), converted-or-discarded immediately (no raw JSON accumulation)
data_pull.note_on_high_match_rate: not overmatching on generic strings (spot-checked: 64 distinct, plausible real leaderboard names, e.g. 'Dominic Peel', 'Majkel1337', 'flg') -- the live ladder's active game population is dominated by its most frequent (generally strongest) players, so a top-150 identity filter still captured 97% of a sequential file sample
data_pull.critical_bug_found_and_fixed: the original Week-1 speculative parser paired each step's action with that SAME step's observation. Real data (hand-validated against a downloaded file, 127/127 decisions cross-checked against build_candidates with 0 mismatches) shows the action at tick i responds to tick (i-1)'s observation for that player -- an off-by-one that would have silently corrupted every extracted decision had it shipped unverified.

archetype_findings.headline: Crustle (the ex-attacker counter this session already found and patched lucario_fighting against) appears in 4 of 26 unique real top-player decks (15.4%) -- not a hypothetical threat, a card ranked competitors are actually running.
other_real_archetypes_seen: Team Rocket's Mewtwo ex / Articuno / Tarountula-Spidops shell (5-6 decks each)
Dragapult ex line (3 decks) -- matches a meta archetype the original planning material named
archetype_findings.our_own_archetype_representation: 0 of 26 unique captured decks contain Mega Lucario ex (678) or Riolu (333) -- lucario_fighting has zero presence among the top-150 leaderboard players sampled this pull.

bc_replay.note: lower than self-play-derived checkpoints' typical ~90%+ -- expected, since predicting varied real players' choices across many different decks is inherently harder than predicting one deterministic heuristic

bc_replay_blend.mix_caveat: load_records shuffles by FILE, not by weighted source; selfplay_v1 has ~16x more files than replays (16000 vs 994), so the naive multi-directory blend is heavily self-play-dominated, not a balanced 50/50 mix. This is a real methodological limitation of the simple approach taken, noted rather than hidden.

bc_replay_blend_vs_teacher_bc_text.verdict: tie, CI includes 50% -- not a decisive win despite the favorable point estimate

bench_replay_vs_existing.diagnosis: bc_replay's collapse is explained by deck mismatch, not by real-player imitation being a bad idea: 0 of the 26 real decks captured this pull contain Mega Lucario ex or Riolu, so bc_replay was trained entirely on players piloting archetypes our engine has never run and then forced onto lucario_fighting at bench time -- a severe out-of-distribution deployment. bc_replay_blend avoids collapse because it's 91.8% in-distribution self-play data by accident of the naive blend, not because the real-data signal was integrated well.
bench_replay_vs_existing.gate_result: Per this project's standing gate (only fuzz/ship a checkpoint that clears a real, CI-backed win over bc_text), neither new checkpoint clears the bar. Neither was fuzzed or is recommended for the live submission.

recommendation_for_next_session.headline: Real-ladder imitation learning is validated as a real, working pipeline (parser correctness confirmed, real identity matching works, real archetype data extracted) -- but it only pays off when applied to a deck the real data actually represents. lucario_fighting has zero representation among 26 real top-150 decks captured.
options: Filter future pulls specifically for players running an ex/Mega-ex Fighting-type deck close to lucario_fighting, if any exist elsewhere in the corpus -- a fair apples-to-apples imitation test.

Switch the submitted deck to one of the real, popular, evidence-backed archetypes found this pull (e.g. the Team Rocket's Mewtwo ex shell, seen in 5-6 of 26 real decks) and imitate real players who actually ran it -- a larger pivot, not something auto-executed without explicit sign-off given it replaces the deck this whole session's Weeks 0-3 work was built around.
Fix the blend ratio properly (weight by source, not by file count) before drawing any conclusion about whether real data helps when mixed with self-play.
